# 08 — Observability, Testing & QA

Reviewer 08 of 10. All memongo claims verified against executing source code (repo-root-relative `file:line`). Competitor claims verified against GitHub source trees via the GitHub API. Everything else is marked UNVERIFIED.

## 1. Executive summary (top 5 findings, one line each)

1. CI never runs 27 existing, passing API tests — including `apps/api/src/contract-conformance.test.ts`, the OpenAPI drift guard that six source files claim "fails CI" — because `apps/api/package.json:12` lists test files explicitly and omits it (verified passing when run manually).
2. 203 test cases across 21 files under `scripts/` (benchmark harness, LLM-judge decoy calibration, memory-eval core, publishability policy) are wired to no CI workflow or package script — the quality-critical tests are dead code in CI.
3. A fully tested secret-redaction utility (`packages/lib/src/redact.ts:39`) is called by zero production log paths; raw user queries (`packages/memory-engine/src/mongodb-search-v2.ts:1688`) and raw driver errors that can embed Mongo URIs (`apps/api/src/lib/errors.ts:66`) reach logs unredacted.
4. The nightly "Full E2E" gate can pass green with every embedding/LLM suite skipped: pervasive `describe.skipIf` + no skipped-count guard, and the repo's own `packages/memory-engine/vitest.config.ts` documents a real 190-tests-skipped "green" incident.
5. Production is an observability island: no OTel/prometheus/driver command monitoring anywhere, and the DB-native telemetry (p50/p95/p99 per operation) is written on every call but its aggregation API is unreachable from the bridge, API, MCP, or web console.

## 3. Correctness bugs (reasoned reproductions, not speculation)

**B1 — CI test script excludes two existing, passing test files, killing the OpenAPI contract guard.**
`apps/api/package.json:12` is `"test": "vitest run src/app.test.ts src/app.segment*.test.ts"`. The package contains seven test files; this script runs five. Excluded: `apps/api/src/contract-conformance.test.ts` (9 cases) and `apps/api/src/lib/validation.test.ts` (18 cases). I ran both manually: `2 passed (2), Tests 27 passed (27)`. So the exclusion is accidental, not known-broken. Consequence: `packages/lib/src/contract.ts` and five `apps/api/src/openapi-paths-*.ts` files state in code comments that "contract-conformance.test.ts fails CI when the spec drifts" — that guard has not executed in CI for the life of this script. Any OpenAPI/router drift, and any validation-regression in `lib/validation.ts`, lands silently. Reproduction: `cd apps/api && bun run test` and observe vitest's file list (5 files), vs `git ls-files 'src/**/*.test.ts'` (7 files).

**B2 — 203 test cases under `scripts/` are wired to nothing.**
`scripts/` contains 21 `*.test.ts` files / 203 cases (counted), including the benchmark harness's own tests (`scripts/benchmark/*.test.ts` — runner, readiness, parity envelope, checkpoint, retry), the LLM-judge calibration tests (`scripts/mongodb-e2e-qa.test.ts`: judgeAnswer degradation, decoy FPR), `scripts/memory-eval-core.test.ts`, `scripts/run-benchmark.test.ts`, and `scripts/check-publishability.test.ts`. No `.github/workflows/*` step, no package `test` script, and no turbo task executes them (`turbo.json` defines `test`/`test:e2e` over workspace packages only; `scripts/` is not a workspace — root `package.json` workspaces are `apps/*` and `packages/*`). These tests can rot to red without anyone noticing, which is precisely the state in which a QA harness becomes untrustworthy.

**B3 — The nightly full-E2E gate can report green with zero assertions executed.**
Virtually every key- or provider-gated e2e suite uses `describe.skipIf` (e.g., `packages/memory-engine/src/e2e-evaluation.e2e.test.ts:327,1554,1577` — ten phases gated on `HAS_REAL_EMBEDDINGS`; `mongodb-contradiction.e2e.test.ts:84`, `mongodb-temporal-extraction.e2e.test.ts`, `mongodb-relation-extraction.e2e.test.ts`, `mongodb-consolidation-reasoning.e2e.test.ts` gated on an LLM provider; `real-e2e-v2.e2e.test.ts` and `mongodb-embedding-coverage.e2e.test.ts` gated on the Voyage key). Vitest exits 0 when tests are skipped. `.github/workflows/e2e-nightly.yml` supplies `VOYAGE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.VOYAGE_API_KEY }}` (:24,:50) and asserts nothing about executed-vs-skipped counts. If that secret is missing, rotated, or renamed, the "Full E2E against real MongoDB" job passes with every embedding/LLM suite skipped. This is not hypothetical: `packages/memory-engine/vitest.config.ts:14-38` documents a real incident where a run "reported 190 skipped tests, which reads as 'green with some gaps' instead of 'two of the largest suites never executed'" — the fix scaled timeouts but no guard against skip-green was added at the workflow level.

**B4 — Secret/PII redaction is implemented, tested, and connected to zero production log paths.**
`packages/lib/src/redact.ts:39` exports `redactSensitiveText` covering API keys, bearer tokens, PEM blocks, `sk-`/`ghp_`/`npm_` prefixes, and credentials-bearing connection strings (pattern at `redact.ts:20`); `packages/lib/src/redact.test.ts` exercises it thoroughly. Grep for `redactSensitiveText` outside its own test and the lib barrel export: zero call sites. Meanwhile: (a) `packages/lib/src/logger.ts:55` `formatLine` serializes meta with plain `JSON.stringify` — no redaction hook; (b) `apps/api/src/lib/errors.ts:66` `internalError` logs raw `err.message` and `err.stack` — MongoDB driver network errors routinely embed the connection string with credentials, which is exactly what the dead pattern at `redact.ts:20` was written for; (c) `packages/memory-engine/src/mongodb-search-v2.ts:1688` and `mongodb-retrieval-planner.ts:1063` log the raw user query at error level — user memory content/PII in operational logs; (d) `apps/mcp/src/server.ts:1231` prints raw error objects. Reproduction: issue a search whose query contains an `sk-`-shaped example token against an engine with a failing lane; the full token appears in the log line via `{ query, error }`.

## 4. Unknown unknowns (things no checklist covers — HIGHEST VALUE)

**U1 — Observability data island: metrics are written but cannot be read through the product.**
The telemetry pipeline is real and well built (per-op docs, TTL, $percentile aggregations — `packages/memory-engine/src/mongodb-telemetry.ts:60-190`), but `getLatencyStats`/`getCacheHitRate`/`getOperationDistribution` are consumed only by tests (`real-e2e-v2.e2e.test.ts`, `mongodb-telemetry.test.ts`). The bridge exports nothing telemetry-related (grep `packages/memory-bridge/src` — zero hits), the API route surface has no metrics endpoint (`apps/api/src/openapi-paths-*.ts`), and the web console never fetches them (`apps/web` grep — only marketing copy mentions telemetry). An operator running memongo in production has no way to see p95 search latency or cache hit rate without direct database access. Combined with zero OTel/prometheus (checklist #6) and zero MongoDB driver command monitoring (the Node driver exposes `commandStarted`/`commandFailed`/SDAM/pool events; grep shows no subscription anywhere), a senior mem0/letta/zep engineer would be shocked at how little of this system is observable in flight.

**U2 — No read/audit trail at the API layer for a multi-tenant memory product.**
`requestId()` middleware exists (`apps/api/src/app.ts:549`) but the id is only ever emitted on 500/503 failures (`apps/api/src/lib/errors.ts:66`). Successful reads (search, recall, context-bundle, state) and writes are not logged at all at the API layer — no record of which key/tenant read whose memory when. Engine-side, `memory_mutations` records create/update/delete/invalidate mutations (`packages/memory-engine/src/mongodb-mutations.ts`), and `access_events` feed relevance ranking — but access events expire in 30 days (`mongodb-schema-standard-indexes-core.ts` accessEvents TTL, asserted in `mongodb-schema.part3.test.ts`) and are a ranking signal, not a security audit. For a system whose entire value is cross-session personal data, there is no compliance-grade audit log, and no test asserting one because none exists.

**U3 — Property-based testing is decorative.**
`fast-check` is a root devDependency (`package.json` devDependencies), and the only test using it is `packages/memory-engine/src/fast-check-smoke.test.ts`, which asserts `n + 0 === n` over 10 runs. Zero properties exercise any engine invariant (consolidation idempotency, scope-filter monotonicity, embedding dimension stability, prefix-namespace isolation). The dependency and the file create the appearance of property testing while testing nothing about the product.

**U4 — Coverage is claimed but never measured or gated.**
No vitest coverage configuration exists anywhere (the only vitest config in the repo is `packages/memory-engine/vitest.config.ts`, which sets timeouts only); no CI step collects coverage; no thresholds. The test suite is large (~3,100 cases) but nobody can state what fraction of the engine's branches it executes — coverage is unmeasured, so "tested" and "covered" are indistinguishable in this repo.

**U5 — Releases ship without a single real-MongoDB test or a published-artifact smoke test.**
`.github/workflows/publish.yml` publishes eight packages after `bun run test` (unit only, :35). The secret-free tier-A e2e that gates every PR (`ci.yml` e2e job) is not a publish gate, and nothing after publishing installs `@memongo/memory-engine` from npm and runs a smoke (the prepublish `check-publishability` inspects tarball contents, not runtime behavior). A broken `exports` map or a dist/ build regression ships to users having passed "Test".

**U6 — No bulk erasure capability exists, so the most destructive data operation is untested by construction.**
The full route surface (`apps/api/src/openapi-paths-*.ts`) offers per-item `/v1/lifecycle/delete` only; there is no engine or API path to erase all data for an agent or tenant (grep `eraseAll|purge|wipe|deleteAll` across `packages` and `apps` — zero hits). For a long-term memory product holding personal data, right-to-erasure is a data-lifecycle primitive that competitors expose, and its absence means both a product gap and a permanent QA blind spot (you cannot test what does not exist).

**U7 — MCP spec observability surface is unimplemented.**
The MCP server registers only `tools/list` and `tools/call` request handlers (`apps/mcp/src/server.ts:7-10`); grep for `notifications/message`, `logging`, `setLevel`, `progress` across `apps/mcp/src` — zero hits. Per the MCP specification (server utilities/logging), servers can emit structured log messages with severity that clients control via `logging/setLevel`, and long-running operations should emit `notifications/progress`. Memongo's tools include potentially slow imports (`memongo_import_conversations`) with no progress signal, and its only logging is `console.error` to stderr (`apps/mcp/src/server.ts:1231`, `apps/mcp/src/http-transport.ts:109`). Hosts get a silent black box.

**U8 — Telemetry emit has no sampling, batching, or kill-switch.**
`emitTelemetry` is a fire-and-forget `insertOne` per operation (`packages/memory-engine/src/mongodb-telemetry.ts:60-67`) called unconditionally from every hot path: search (`mongodb-manager-search.ts:724,1114`), cache-check (`mongodb-query-cache.ts`), rerank (`mongodb-reranker.ts`), graph expansion (`mongodb-graph.ts`, 3 sites), query rewrite (`mongodb-query-rewriter.ts`), profile synthesis and active-slate hydration (`mongodb-profile.ts`, `mongodb-active-slate.ts`). The 7-day TTL (`mongodb-schema-validators.ts:165`) bounds storage, not insert load: at production QPS this doubles write traffic to the memory cluster with no way to turn it down without a deploy.

**U9 — /ready's vector lane is a boot-time snapshot, so orchestrators route traffic to a broken search.**
`probeVectorAvailability` returns `this.host.capabilities.vectorSearch` captured when the manager was created (`packages/memory-engine/src/mongodb-manager-admin.ts:616-620`; embedding probe similarly returns cached capability at :596-615). `apps/api/src/lib/readiness.ts:15` admits "Search-index readiness has no bridge-level live signal today." The consequence: mongot can die an hour after boot and /ready keeps returning 200 while every vector search fails — the exact failure mode a readiness probe exists to catch. A cheap live probe (a 1-doc `$vectorSearch` or index-status round trip) is what the "vector probe doubles as the vector-lane signal" fallback claims to be but isn't.

## 6. External docs alignment (MongoDB/MCP/OWASP where relevant)

- **MCP specification (server utilities/logging, 2025-03-26, modelcontextprotocol.io)**: servers may emit `notifications/message` with severity levels; clients control verbosity via `logging/setLevel`; long operations use `notifications/progress`. Memongo implements none of these (`apps/mcp/src/server.ts:7-10` registers only tools handlers; grep zero hits for logging/progress) — misaligned with the spec's observability utilities.
- **MongoDB Node driver monitoring docs (mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node, command monitoring / monitor application events)**: the driver exposes `commandStartedEvent`/`commandSucceededEvent`/`commandFailedEvent`, SDAM events, and connection-pool events for APM. Memongo subscribes to none (repo-wide grep zero hits); all MongoDB failures surface only through per-call `catch` blocks as scattered `log.warn` lines. Misaligned — this is the driver's built-in observability seam and it is unused.
- **OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (LLM02: Sensitive Information Disclosure)**: raw user queries at error level (`packages/memory-engine/src/mongodb-search-v2.ts:1688`) and raw error messages/stacks (`apps/api/src/lib/errors.ts:66`) are logged without redaction, while a purpose-built redaction utility (`packages/lib/src/redact.ts:39`) sits unused. Misaligned — the control exists in the codebase but is not deployed into the logging pipeline.
- **LongMemEval (arXiv 2410.10813, ICLR 2025)**: the official protocol scores LLM-judged answer correctness (J) over 500 questions of 7 types, including abstention. Memongo's longmemeval "officialMetrics" are retrieval metrics — session/turn recall and nDCG, abstention-case counts (`packages/memory-engine/src/types.ts:1067-1088`) — with judged accuracy only in the LOCOMO contract (`scripts/benchmark/benchmark-quality-contracts.ts:36-38`). Partially aligned: the retrieval framing is honest and self-consistent, but memongo's numbers are not comparable to published LongMemEval J scores (e.g., mem0's 94.4 claim), and nothing in the repo computes the official J score for LongMemEval.
- **Vitest best practices (skip semantics)**: skipped tests do not fail a vitest run. Combined with the pervasive `describe.skipIf` gating, any workflow relying on exit code alone (both e2e workflows do) cannot distinguish "all assertions passed" from "all assertions skipped." The repo's own `packages/memory-engine/vitest.config.ts:14-38` documents this exact failure mode occurring in practice.

## 7. Recommendations (P0 = data loss/security, P1 = correctness/cost, P2 = quality)

**P0 (1)**
1. Wire `redactSensitiveText` into every production log path: the logger's `formatLine` meta serialization (`packages/lib/src/logger.ts:55`), the API error envelope (`apps/api/src/lib/errors.ts:66`), and drop raw `{ query }` from `mongodb-search-v2.ts:1688` / `mongodb-retrieval-planner.ts:1063` (log a truncated hash or length instead). Driver error messages can embed credentials and user queries are memory content; today both reach logs unredacted.

**P1 (6)**
1. Fix `apps/api/package.json:12` to run all seven test files (`vitest run src` like the mcp package does) — restores the OpenAPI contract drift guard and 18 validation tests to CI.
2. Wire `scripts/**` tests into CI: a root vitest project or a CI step (`bunx vitest run scripts`) so the 203 benchmark/judge/eval cases actually execute.
3. Add a skip-green guard to both e2e workflows: fail if executed-test count is zero or if suites expected to run were skipped (e.g., assert `resolvePreviewVoyageApiKey()` resolved before invoking `test:e2e` in nightly, and parse the vitest summary for skipped counts).
4. Make tier-A e2e (secret-free, already containerized) and a post-publish npm-install smoke test gates in `.github/workflows/publish.yml`.
5. Make /ready's vector lane a live probe (index-status or single-vector round trip) instead of the creation-time capability snapshot (`packages/memory-engine/src/mongodb-manager-admin.ts:616`; `apps/api/src/lib/readiness.ts:15`).
6. Run at least a sample-mode benchmark plus `scripts/mongodb-e2e-qa.e2e.test.ts` on the nightly schedule, and add LLM-judged answer accuracy to the LongMemEval contract so numbers are comparable to the official protocol (currently retrieval-only, `packages/memory-engine/src/types.ts:1067-1088`).

**P2 (6)**
1. Expose the telemetry aggregations through the bridge and a `/v1/metrics` (or admin) API route, and/or adopt OTel; subscribe to MongoDB driver command-monitoring events for a real APM feed (competitor precedent: getzep/graphiti `graphiti_core/telemetry/telemetry.py`).
2. Implement the MCP `logging` capability (notifications/message + setLevel) and progress notifications for long-running tools (`apps/mcp/src/server.ts`).
3. Add a security/compliance audit log of tenant reads and writes at the API layer (requestId is already generated at `apps/api/src/app.ts:549` but only surfaces on failures).
4. Add sampling/kill-switch env for `emitTelemetry` to avoid doubling write load at high QPS (`packages/memory-engine/src/mongodb-telemetry.ts:60`).
5. Replace the tautological `fast-check-smoke.test.ts` with real properties over engine invariants, and add vitest coverage collection with thresholds so "tested" is measurable.
6. Give `apps/web` any test at all (zero today — `apps/web/package.json` has no test script) and add a bulk agent/tenant erasure capability with tests, closing the GDPR-shaped product and QA hole.
